tasks.short: Write each service on the customer card, find customers due for service, check the reminder list, send reminders, phone customers without e-mail, have customers book, and enter the bookings.

steps.what: Service attendant maintains customer records by writing each service on the customer card
Service attendant goes through the cards to find customers due for service
Service attendant checks the reminder list
Service attendant follows up with telephone or mail reminders of services due
Service attendant phones regular customers who have no e-mail or mobile number
Customer phones back to book the service
Service attendant enters the service bookings in the agenda

tasks.design: The till and service system ({OTHER}) records each service against the licence plate and computes the next due date, so cards are not kept or searched. The attendant checks the weekly due list, and once checked, text and e-mail reminders with a booking link go out; regulars without a number or address still get a call. Bookings made through the link land in the agenda.
tasks.previous_blocker: Customer cards were paper and reminders were phone calls one by one.
tasks.enabler_now: Garage systems compute due dates from service records and send reminders with booking links.
tasks.still_hard: Older regulars expect a personal call.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which regular will only book if asked in person.
tasks.altitude: The attendant checks reminders instead of finding and calling every customer.

evidence.claim: Garage service systems can compute due dates from service records and send reminders with booking links.
Service reminders to existing customers use their contact details, which are personal data under the GDPR.

assumptions: Boundary: from the service done to the service booked; the service itself is outside.
Input contract: service intervals set by the station; contact details given by customers; fallback is cards and calls.
Customers book through the link in about the time a call took; priced as customer time.
Calls to regulars without e-mail stay.
research_questions: Do more customers return for service when due?

incremental.description: Service attendant collects e-mail addresses and mobile numbers at the till.
Customers book through the reminder link.

approvals.approved_version: The reminder list as checked by the attendant in s3.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many older regulars who need calls; high: most customers with e-mail or mobile numbers.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Hear the customer's question, give directions from local knowledge, look up road works and closures, and show the route on a map.

steps.what: Customer asks about the road or route
Service attendant provides customers with information about local roads or highways
Service attendant looks up road works and closures
Service attendant shows the route on a paper map

tasks.design: A screen at the counter shows live road works, closures and traffic from the public traffic feed, and a QR code opens the route in the customer's own navigation app, so fewer routes are drawn on paper maps. Giving directions from local knowledge stays with the attendant.
tasks.previous_blocker: Road works were looked up by phone or memory and routes shown on paper maps.
tasks.enabler_now: Public traffic feeds and navigation apps give live road information.
tasks.still_hard: Local shortcuts and tricky junctions are not on any screen.
tasks.human_edge: Warning a caravan driver about a low bridge the app ignores.

reach.learn: Whether the counter screen is used.

evidence.claim: Public traffic feeds show road works, closures and traffic; navigation apps open routes from a link.

assumptions: Boundary: from the customer's question to the route shown; selling maps is outside.
Input contract: road information from the public traffic feed; fallback is local knowledge and paper maps.
Customers open the route on their phone in about the time it took to look at the map; priced as customer time.
Directions from local knowledge do not change.
research_questions: Do customers use the QR route?

incremental.description: Service attendant checks the counter screen works each morning.
Customers open the route on their own phone.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: mostly local regulars; high: a motorway station with many travellers.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The service attendant keeps serving customers and giving local advice; paper cards, reminder calls and paper maps shrink.
role.ambitious_version: An attendant with more time for customers at the pump and counter.
